# Conservation of Nose-Touch Avoidance Across *C. elegans* and Relatives

Nose-touch avoidance was highly conserved in five of the six species tested (Figure 5A). After the first few positive trials, *C. tripartitum* showed an overall avoidance rate of less than 10%, suggesting that it adapts to the nose-touch stimulus faster than *C. elegans* and the other species (Figure 5A). During the first three trials, however, its response was quantitatively similar to that of *C. elegans* (Figure S2 in Additional file 2).

Ablating ASH neurons in five nose-touch-responsive species resulted in the loss of nose-touch avoidance (Figure 5A). Four of the five species still showed responses in 20–30% of trials, but *Caenorhabditis* sp. 3 was unique: its ASH-ablated animals showed no response to nose touch (Figure 5A).

Ablation of the AWC neuron did not affect nose-touch responses in the different species (Figure S3 in Additional file 2).

In profile, the petiole has an elongate peduncle and a well-developed node. The node’s dorsum slopes downward posteriorly, producing a short posterior face. Subject: Key Findings on foxl2 Expression Patterns in Trout

Dear Customer,

We are pleased to share a summary of our findings on foxl2 transcript expression in your study.

Both foxl2 transcripts were expressed very early in development (Figure 2). In males, foxl2a expression was highly restricted, whereas the diverged paralog foxl2b was present in most adult extragonadal tissues examined (see Additional file 2).

In adult females, foxl2b expression was highly restricted, essentially confined to the skin, gill, and ovary. Expression of foxl2b was also very strong in the testis, consistent with previous findings that foxl2b was present and foxl2a was absent in later stages of testis development in trout [23].

Together, these results suggest that foxl2b may be a critical regulator of male-specific genes, such as cyp19b1, particularly later in development.

Thank you for your time and interest in our research.

Best regards,

We derived a time-dependent mild-slope equation based on the formal derivation of Smith & Sprinks (1975). From it, we obtained the higher-order dispersion relation for waves over uneven bottoms.

Using only linear dispersion for steady waves, we recovered equation (2.12) of Chamberlain & Porter (1995), known as the Modified Mild-Slope Equation (MMSE). For the leading-order solution, the modified curvature terms of the MMSE have significant effects, while the slope-squared terms remain negligible, consistent with the mild-slope assumption. We therefore retained all the modified curvature terms neglected in the MSE, leading to a uniform model.

We developed a numerical model using the finite element method (FEM) to predict wave scattering over a varying bottom. The uniform model generally predicts salient wave features over various seabeds, including sinusoidal beds and man-made bars. For sinusoidal beds, its results agree more closely with experimental data than those of other established models. For man-made bars, the results of both the MMSE and the uniform model agree more closely with experimental data than those of Kirby (1986).

An important application of the FEM model is the transformation of waves over arbitrarily varying bathymetry.

We want to share some important information about early hearing development. People typically develop spoken language within the first few years of life. Hearing impairment can affect both the ability to speak and the ability to understand spoken language.

By the time a severe hearing impairment becomes apparent in a deaf child, communication difficulties may already have caused problems within the family and hindered the child’s social skills. These challenges can be reduced if the child is part of a Deaf community where sign language is used instead of spoken language (please see our article on Deaf Culture).

In many developed countries, newborns are evaluated for hearing impairment to prevent a deaf child from being inadvertently isolated within a hearing family. Although sign language is a complete means of communication, literacy ultimately depends on the ability to understand speech. In the vast majority of written language, symbols represent the sounds of words.

A person who hears well enough to learn to speak and read will retain the ability to read even if their hearing later becomes too impaired to hear voices. However, a person who never heard well enough to learn to speak is rarely able to read proficiently (see [4]). Most evidence suggests that identifying hearing impairment early is key to helping a child with very insensitive hearing learn spoken language effectively. Listening also plays an important role in learning a second language.

**Transduction** is the conversion of physical and chemical signals into neural impulses. In the nervous system, it is the fundamental process by which stimuli are translated into electrical signals. In sensory transduction, specialized sensory receptors transform physical or chemical inputs into electrical impulses that travel to the brain.

The **visual system** provides an example. In the retina, **rod and cone cells** connect the physical environment to neural communication. When light strikes these photoreceptors, it triggers a conformational change in the protein **rhodopsin**. This change sets off a cascade of events that alters the photoreceptor’s electrochemical gradient. As the gradient decreases, so do the electrical signals transmitted to the brain. In other words, **more light hitting the photoreceptor results in fewer electrical impulses**, allowing the brain to decode the visual world.

🎮 **Mobile Gaming: The Next Evolution of Co-Creation**

Mobile internet is expanding the immersive potential of storytelling through electronic games played on portable, location-aware interfaces. These games are the latest step in a decades-long evolution toward giving players a role not just as avatars in a gameworld, but as co-authors alongside the original designers.

Location-aware interfaces allow players to bring physical places into the gameworld and the gameworld into physical places—a first for interactive media. Mobile games also move beyond linear narratives, favoring cooperative storytelling that draws on each player’s experience of place.

The idea of the “author-player” as a worldmaker is not new, but mobile games take it beyond the constraints of traditional video games. By extending worldmaking beyond the screen and into the physical world, location-aware interfaces use players’ sensory experiences of real places as storytelling tools.

In our essay, we theorize about the unique storytelling potential of mobile games and describe our experience trying to harness it through the design and implementation of our hybrid-reality game, **University of Death**.

Below are the key findings from our analysis of lung tissue volume and functional changes.

Total lung tissue volume was calculated as the number of voxels multiplied by the volume of each voxel, provided the compartment considered had a CT number above zero.

The change in functional residual capacity following PEEP withdrawal (ΔFRC) was calculated as the difference in total gas volume in the whole lung between PEEP and ZEEP. Alveolar derecruitment was defined as the difference in gas volume within poorly aerated and nonaerated lung regions between these conditions.

We also calculated changes in gas volume following PEEP withdrawal in normally aerated lung regions, defined by CT attenuations between -500 and -900 HU (see Figure 2).

As described in reference [21], the distribution of lost lung aeration for each patient (lung morphology) was classified as diffuse, patchy, or lobar based on the distribution of CT attenuations at ZEEP.

Subject: Tips for Hitchhiking in the Ruhr Area, Germany

Dear Customer,

The Ruhr Area (German: Ruhrgebiet), often called the Ruhr, is an urban region in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It includes many former industrial cities: Duisburg, Oberhausen, Bottrop, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Bochum, Herne, Hamm, Hagen, Dortmund, Recklinghausen, Unna, and Witten.

The region has a population of about five million, making it significantly larger than Berlin, Hamburg, or Munich. Although it has a dense motorway network, hitchhiking can be difficult because of the complex network of smaller roads. The main motorways serving the region are the A1, A2, and A3.

If you plan to hitchhike here, try to stay on these main motorways. The smaller roads have very little transit traffic and can be extremely difficult to navigate. Germany is generally a pleasant place to hitchhike, but the Ruhr Area is by far the most unpleasant part of the country for it.

Hitchhiking within the Ruhr Area is much like hitchhiking in a large city such as Istanbul. The cities are independent, but to travelers they can feel like districts of one massive city.

We hope this information helps you plan a safe and enjoyable trip.

Best regards,
